one_line_contribution: A token-matched and format-matched control for agentic experience memory showing the per-query read is inert -- correctly retrieved top-k (A1(7)) buys no more than decoys retrieved for a different query (A2(7)) or a single fixed prefix identical across all queries (A3(7)), and no more than a bank compiled offline into one instruction (P1) -- with a measured experience-following rate to establish that the injected text is read yet valueless, rather than ignored.
closest_prior_work: The threat the proposal never names is the in-context-learning demonstration-selection literature, not the agentic-memory literature it surveys. Min et al. 2022 ('Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations') is the same dissociation the proposal calls its centerpiece: models condition on demonstration format and input distribution while the correctness of the demonstration content contributes little, i.e. following without benefit. Cuconasu et al. 2024 ('The Power of Noise') is the same decoy arm: random/irrelevant retrieved passages substituted at matched count do not degrade, and can improve, RAG accuracy. Liu et al. 2022 and the retrieval-vs-random exemplar comparisons that followed made 'retrieved-for-this-query vs random-at-equal-k' a standard ICL protocol years ago. That does not fully preempt the proposal -- self-collected multi-step trajectories in a sequential environment are a different object from labeled QA exemplars, Yoo et al. 2022 showed Min et al.'s null weakens with scale and task type, and A3(7)'s prefix-cacheability argument is genuinely new -- but it converts the contribution from 'a control nobody has run' to 'a known ICL control transplanted to agent memory,' which is a much smaller claim than the abstract makes. On the constructive side Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952) already own compilation-as-method, and the proposal correctly concedes this; the residual novelty is entirely in the A1/A2/A3 conditioning block and the ExpeL B1-B5 decomposition.
strongest_objection: The conditioning claim is likely vacuous by construction, and nothing in the pre-registration prevents it. This track's own prior measured result is that injecting seven retrieved items fixed zero instances and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031 and p=0.016, replicated), and that cutting seven to three removed the harm. The proposal then makes k=7 the load-bearing configuration for predictions 1-3. If A1(7) does not beat A0 above the measured noise floor -- which the track's own pilot says is the expected outcome at exactly this k -- then A1(7) ~ A2(7) ~ A3(7) demonstrates only that three ways of adding useless tokens are equally useless. The paper would then be entitled to say 'the memory channel is inert at 14B,' a weaker and partly already-reported claim, but not 'the query-conditioning is inert,' which requires there to be something for conditioning to have been responsible for. Prediction 1's own escape clause exposes this: 'at least 80% of whatever advantage correct retrieval holds over A0 survives replacement by decoys' is a ratio whose denominator (A1(7) - A0) is expected to be zero or negative, making the criterion undefined rather than lenient. Prediction 7 does not patch the hole, because it gates on P1 - P0 (the compiled bank beating bank-blind optimization), not on the injected bank ever having worked. Compounding this, the pre-registered TOST margin of +/-3 points on WebShop is the same magnitude as the gains ExpeL, AWM and A-Mem report; passing equivalence at +/-3 bounds the retrieval channel at roughly the size its advocates already claim for it, so the headline 'ExpeL's ablation row should not survive a token-matched control' is not licensed by the test as specified.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register a positive-control gate: the conditioning claim is reported only if A1(7) - A0 (or, failing that, A5 - A0) exceeds the 95th-percentile null-replicate floor in that environment; otherwise the paper reports 'the injected memory channel is inert at this scale' and drops the conditioning framing, exactly as it already commits to do for the P1 ~ P0 case. Relatedly, run the conditioning block at the dev-tuned k* rather than fixing k=7, so the retrieval arm is evaluated at its best configuration and not at the value this track already measured as harmful. (2) Tighten the equivalence margin to below the effect sizes the target papers claim -- roughly +/-0.015 WebShop reward and +/-2 points EM -- and re-derive n, or state explicitly in the abstract that the result bounds the channel at, not below, the published claim sizes. Note also that applying Holm across the ten-row conditioning family to TOST tests inflates the effective margin further and needs to be handled explicitly. (3) Add the missing arm below. (4) Add a single 32B point (the track budget explicitly allows ~32B on 4xA100); with only 8B and 14B, 'conditioning becomes useful at frontier scale' is not merely unexcluded, it is the reviewer's default reading. (5) Cite and position against Min et al. 2022 and Cuconasu et al. 2024; the gap statement is currently a claim about the agentic-memory subfield being unaware of a control that ICL has run for years.
missing_baseline: P1 + live top-k retrieval at inference: the compiled, bank-derived instruction held fixed with the retrieval channel simply switched on. This is what a practitioner does when adding memory to an already-optimized prompt, and it is the only clean test of 'retrieval adds nothing on top of compilation.' As specified, P2 vs P1 confounds the channel with a differently-optimized instruction (P2's instruction was evolved against retrieval, P1's was not), and P2 vs P3 holds the instruction fixed but only swaps content, never removes it -- so no contrast in the grid isolates the marginal value of retrieval given a compiled instruction. It costs 500 additional episodes. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also press: an A1 arm at the dev-tuned k* alongside A1(7), and one open-weight model above 14B.
preprint_collision: This is a better-than-average check -- nine queries, a named hard collision (Atlas, arXiv:2603.15666) with an argued and falsifiable distinction, a named counter-hypothesis (arXiv:2606.06036), and an explicit correction retracting prior-round citations -- but it undercuts itself in two specific ways. First, it discloses that five citations load-bearing in the previous round (MemHarness 2607.28272, RecMem 2605.16045, AtomicRAG 2604.20844, Distractor-Aware Truncation 2608.03297, and 'Decocted Experience' 2604.04373, previously flagged as the closest threat) could not be re-found this round and were removed. A search instrument whose returns do not replicate between rounds cannot support a gap statement, and the current round's unverified items -- Auto-Dreamer 2605.20616, Structured Distillation 2603.13017, and Atlas itself, whose venue and authorship the author admits could not be confirmed -- inherit exactly that doubt. The honest reading is that the sole named hard collision may be a mirage in either direction, and the proposal cannot presently tell which. Second, and more damagingly, all nine queries appear to be phrased over agentic memory; none searched the ICL demonstration-selection space (retrieved vs random exemplars at matched k, ground-truth-label ablations), which is where the predicted null is closest to already-established. I did not find a preprint that runs the exact A1/A2/A3 grid inside a published agentic-memory system, so predictions 1-3 and 6 are probably still open; but the gap statement as written overclaims, because it establishes only that one subfield has not run a control that a neighboring subfield made routine.
